title: Jerusalem without walls; flee from Babylon; many nations joined to the LORD (Zech 2:4–13)
speaker: The LORD (through the angel and the prophet)
description: Jerusalem will overflow its walls and the LORD will be its wall of fire; the exiles must flee the land of the north and escape from Babylon; the plunderers will become plunder; the LORD will dwell in Zion, many nations will join themselves to him, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
in_text_interpretation: The text states the purposes but names no date or agent.

interpretations.label: Partial fulfilment in the Persian-era resettlement; ultimate fulfilment in the Messiah's reign
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the promises of overflowing population and divine protection exceed the small post-exilic city. Historical evidence: Jerusalem was resettled and its walls rebuilt under Nehemiah (Neh 2–6; 11). Guzik sees the ultimate fulfilment in the Messiah's future reign. Objection: the wall-less city of 2:4 stands in tension with Nehemiah's rebuilding of the walls.

referents.referent: Restored Jerusalem, ultimately under the Messiah
